reader.requirement: At --std 85, FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION({argument-1}...) returns an (implementor-precision) approximation of the population standard deviation of the argument-1 series, for literals, items of any numeric usage, expressions and table(ALL) arguments in one or more dimensions, ODO included.

edition-consulted.switches: D8 edition window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 for the 1989 module rows, IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel; COBOL1502/1503 outside it

ConstructRegistry NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002: at 85 a numeric/integer function written where an identifier stands (MOVE sender) is refused (COBOL0900), per §1989:A.2.3 GR2/GR3; never reached inside an arithmetic expression
Edition.DigitCapacityExcess: 18-digit cap on items and literals at 85 (31 later); bounds the argument range only
num.StandardDecimal (OPTIONS ARITHMETIC, a 2002+ paragraph, so always native at 85): the native dispatch is the one a 2023 program with no ARITHMETIC clause takes

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicBinder.cs, IntrinsicRenderer.cs, IntrinsicCarrierRules.cs, FunctionValueLane.cs for Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|ArithmeticMode|StandardDecimal; the runtime bodies take no edition input
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the native exact-list arm (StdDevExact, then NarrowResult) is the same at 85 and 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover two 18-digit cancelling items, a two-element table(ALL) and SD(1 3); not negative or scaled lists, ODO ALL, two-dimensional ALL, expressions, or the 18-digit extreme

reader.notes: The exact list is formed exactly, rooted at 34 digits, then narrowed to binary64. That is why SD(999999999999999999 -999999999999999999) becomes 1E18 and overflows an S9(18) receiver. The precision is the implementor's under §1989:A.2.3 GR2, so this is a quality lead, not a defect: the exact value fits the edition's largest item. Output was identical at --std 2023.

refuter.evidence: rsd1-002 (--std 85): two-dimensional ODO table DY(ALL ALL)/DY(1 ALL)/DY(ALL 1) -> 5.25/5.25/0 at N=1 and DY(ALL 1) -> 2 at N=2; 18-digit DISPLAY and COMP pair 100000000000000001/...003 -> 1 (no binary64 collapse); three-value list -> .942809041, and the same with a float-valued member A1 + FUNCTION SIN(0) -> .942809041; negative 18-digit DISPLAY/COMP-3 pair -> .5; literal list -2 -4 -6 -> 1.632993161. '- 2 - 4 - 6' is one arithmetic expression (one value) -> 0, correct parsing. rref1-001: floating literal argument refused at 85; rplace1-001: SUBTRACT FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION(X 1) FROM R refused COBOL0900. The 1E18 narrowing of SD(999999999999999999 -999999999999999999) the reader noted is within the approximation the implementor defines (§1989:A.2.3 GR2). cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.41.4 RV2  (2.41.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV2'.
